zh.title: 西南航空全國性系統當機 登機門人員改以人工處理旅客
zh.summary: 西南航空發生全國性系統當機；登機門人員改以人工方式處理旅客；報導稱再度引發技術可靠性疑問
body: Simple Flying報導，西南航空（Southwest Airlines）發生全國性系統當機，員工被迫以人工方式處理旅客。
報導指出，登機門人員被迫以人工方式處理旅客。
該報導稱，這起事件再度引發對西南航空技術可靠性的疑問。
目前可取得的資料僅為Simple Flying的標題與摘要，未提供當機發生時間、受影響機場、航班數量或旅客處理結果等細節。
報導未說明當機原因，也未提及是否有航班取消、延誤或安全影響，相關資訊仍待進一步確認。

en.title: Southwest Airlines gate agents process passengers manually after nationwide system outage
en.summary: Southwest Airlines nationwide system outage; gate agents processed passengers manually; report says technology reliability questions revived
body: Simple Flying reported that a nationwide system outage forced Southwest Airlines employees to process passengers manually.
According to the report, gate agents were forced to process passengers manually.
The report said the incident revived questions about the airline's technology reliability.

The available material is limited to the Simple Flying headline and summary; it does not state when the outage occurred, which airports were affected, how many flights or passengers were involved, or how the manual processing was carried out.
The report did not state a cause for the outage and did not mention cancellations, delays or safety effects, leaving those details unconfirmed.

zh.title: IATA：人員、技術與全球標準協力推進航空安全
zh.summary: IATA呼籲人員、技術與全球標準協力推進航空安全改善。
body: IATA表示，航空安全下一階段的進展將來自人員、技術與標準更緊密協作，形成具韌性的整體系統。IATA安全事務主管Mark Searle在伊斯坦堡舉行的IATA World Safety and Operations Conference 2026開幕時發表上述看法。
Searle表示，致命事故率已從每3.5 million flights發生一次事故，改善至每5.6 million flights發生一次。IATA並指出，航空安全許多重大挑戰源於標準執行與監督不一致，而非缺少全球標準。
談到技術，Searle表示，全球導航衛星系統（GNSS）幹擾增加，提醒業界技術必須搭配備援、程序、訓練及人員判斷。

en.title: IATA Calls for People, Technology and Standards to Advance Aviation Safety
en.summary: IATA calls for closer coordination of people, technology and global standards to improve aviation safety.
body: IATA said the next advances in aviation safety will depend on people, technology and standards working together as a resilient system. Mark Searle, IATA’s Director of Safety, made the remarks at the opening of the IATA World Safety and Operations Conference 2026 in Istanbul.

Searle said fatal accident rates improved from one accident per 3.5 million flights to one per 5.6 million flights. IATA also said many of aviation’s biggest safety challenges stem from inconsistent implementation and oversight, rather than a lack of global standards.
On technology, Searle said rising Global Navigation Satellite System interference is a reminder that technology must be supported by redundancy, procedures, training and human judgment.
